title: quantization NaN incident breadcrumbs - maya
content:
Summary:
- Intermittent NaNs observed when running int8/FP8 quantized variants of the new gated-attention model on prod-like input traces. BF16 and FP32 runs are stable.
- Repro is flaky but I can trigger it ~1/10 runs with current config. Logs point to NaN in token logits (post-softmax) and occasional CUDA errors in conv/linear kernels.

Repro steps (what I ran locally):
1) Model conversion (reference):
   python tools/convert_quant.py --model checkpoints/gated-attn/step-1 --out artifacts/gated-attn-int8 --quant int8 --calib-data data/calib/1000.jsonl --per-channel True
2) Quick infer:
   CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python examples/run_infer.py --model artifacts/gated-attn-int8 --input test_prompts/long_context.jsonl --dtype int8 --batch 1 --max-tokens 512 --use-kv-cache True
3) Also tried fp8:
   python tools/convert_quant.py --quant fp8 --quant-config configs/fp8-default.yaml
   python examples/run_infer.py --model artifacts/gated-attn-fp8 --dtype fp8 ...

Commands/log snippets (copied from terminal):
- Runtime: 2026-03-08 21:12:34 | INFO | running inference on batch 0
- WARNING: kernel numerical instability detected, fallback to fp32 for layer 42
- RuntimeError: output contains NaN (logits) at token_index=12, step=0
- [CUDA ERROR] kernel launch failed: unspecified launch failure
- Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "examples/run_infer.py", line 198, in <module>
      out = model.generate(batch)
    File "serving_runtime/engine.py", line 124, in generate
      logits = self.forward_step(inputs)

Quick hypothesis list (very initial):
- Calibration distribution mismatch: calibration set too small or not representative (we used 1000 short prompts; production has many long-context prompts with url/text noise).
- Per-tensor quantization for some linear layers underestimates per-channel variances, causing large outliers -> overflow/NaN in matmul kernels.
- LayerNorm/scale parameters quantized incorrectly (should keep LayerNorm and RMSNorm in fp32/bf16).
- Activation outliers: gating or residual add leads to spikes not seen in calib set.
- KV cache accumulation: quantized KV caches lose precision over long sequences, amplify small numerical errors -> NaN.
- Backend kernel bug with FP8 implementation on current CUDA + driver combo (observed a kernel fallback message earlier).

What I tried so far (results):
1) Increase calib set (1000 -> 10k, mixed lengths): reduced frequency from 1/10 to 1/50 but not eliminated.
2) Switch per-channel quantization for all Linear/Conv weights: improved stability; NaNs still occur rarely.
3) Exclude LayerNorm/RMSNorm from quantization (keep fp32): highest impact, NaNs dropped ~90% (suggests norm scale/affine quantization problem).
4) Keep KV cache in fp32 (serialize/deserialize from fp32 but use int8 weights): NaNs still possible but less frequent for very long contexts (>1024 tokens).
5) Try bf16 for all activations + int8 weights: stable so far in stress test (1000 long prompts).
6) Swap to alternate FP8 config (different exponent bias / dynamic range settings): no clear improvement; occasional kernel fallback same as before.
7) Run with TORCH_CHECKS enabled and light debug prints: observed very large activation (~1e5) right before NaN on some failing traces.

Narrowing down layer(s):
- Failing runs often show layer index ~40-46 in the logs. Those correspond to the first attention block after local-window attention (model layout notes in confluence doc).
- Hypothesis: gating nonlinearity (GEGLU/Gated GELU variant) in that block produces high-magnitude activations when fed long HTML-like tokens with consecutive <code> blocks (we saw this in failing prompts).
- Plan: add per-layer activation clipping / outlier detection for the suspected blocks.

Immediate experiments to run (todo):
- [ ] Re-run conversion with clip-threshold=10 for activations on blocks 40-46 and test 2k long-context prompts.
- [ ] Conservative path: force LayerNorm, RMSNorm, and gating projection to bf16 (weights/activations) and keep the rest int8.
- [ ] Gather per-layer activation histograms during inference (save to /tmp/act-hists/) for both calib and prod traces and compare 99.9th pctiles.
- [ ] Try alternative calibration method: KL-divergence vs min-max; test with calib size 20k and mixed-length distribution.
- [ ] Try symmetric vs asymmetric quantization and see which is more robust for gating projections.
- [ ] Run same model on a different machine with driver CUDA 12.2 to rule out kernel bug.

Notes on reproducibility:
- Seeds: torch.manual_seed(42) used but NaN still non-deterministic (depends on input).
- When I force deterministic CUDA behavior, performance degrades and NaNs still appear sometimes (suggests numerical instability, not random race).

Related artifacts / where I looked:
- conversion script: tools/convert_quant.py (added a couple debug flags 2026-03-07)
- serving runtime: serving_runtime/quantize.py and serving_runtime/kernels/fp8_kernels.cu
- calibration config: configs/quant/calib-1000.jsonl and configs/calib/fp8-default.yaml
- failing prompt examples: data/fails/long_html_001.jsonl (attached to the JIRA ticket)

Immediate next steps (actionable for team):
- Jordan: help instrument per-layer activation hist and add an optional clip op during convert (small PR).
- Carlos: try running the failing model on a host with CUDA 12.2 + driver X.Y (we suspect a kernel fallback issue).
- Me (Maya): iterate on calibration (KL + bigger dataset) and try asymmetric per-channel quant for gating projections; collect run logs + activation dumps.

Notes / random observations (brain dump):
- BF16 seems very forgiving; maybe we should ship a hybrid: bf16 for norms/gates and int8 for majority of matmuls. Performance may still be good if we keep critical ops in bf16.
- Might be worth adding a quick-mode during conversion that sanity-checks activations on a holdout set and refuses to output quant artifacts if 99.99th pctile > threshold. Saves production headaches.
- If this is an FP8 backend bug, short-term mitigation: pin fp8 models to newer driver or disable fp8 in Dedicated until we confirm.

References and quick links: (copied here so I don't forget)
- JIRA-INC-987 (main incident ticket)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/456 (wip: debug activations)
- Confluence: confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/quantization-notes

Logs/attachments saved to: /mnt/workspace/maya/quant-debug/2026-03-08/

If I don't get to this tomorrow, next person: follow the todo list above and attach any new histograms to the JIRA ticket.

-- Maya
